subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlinks to selected OpenClaw-home sibling directories, and which subdirectories are safe to inject into startup prompt context?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent behavior changes a filesystem trust boundary for model-visible prompt context and cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Approve a narrow external-bootstrap policy
options.body: Allow only explicit safe bootstrap-content roots or symlink-hop-only cases, while denying credentials, sessions, caches, logs, and direct arbitrary OpenClaw-home paths.

options.title: Keep workspace-root-only reads
options.body: Reject this deployment pattern and document copy or sync-file workflows as the supported safe alternative.

options.title: Fold into the broader symlink PR
options.body: Let the existing maintainer PR own this only if it is expanded to cover the OpenClaw-home policy and security tests explicitly.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow external-bootstrap policy
recommendation.body: Allow only explicit safe bootstrap-content roots or symlink-hop-only cases, while denying credentials, sessions, caches, logs, and direct arbitrary OpenClaw-home paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They left the current maintainer direction on the issue and own the overlapping bootstrap symlink PR.
